changes.detail: The Vue build copies every `.ts` helper a page reaches into its generated tree, but it found them with a regex that only matched `import … from`. A helper reached only through a re-export (`export { x } from './y'` or `export * from './y'`) was never copied, so the build failed with `Could not resolve: "./y"` and every page above it answered 500 in dev. Dependencies are now read with Bun's import scanner, which sees imports, dynamic imports and all three re-export forms; a regex that also covers re-exports is the fallback for source that does not parse.
changes.summary: Vue pages that reach a helper through a re-export build again

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS accepted `@absolutejs/auth` only below 0.77, so a project that added a current auth (0.77 to 0.96) got two copies: its own, plus 0.76.3 nested under AbsoluteJS for the mobile shell. The duplicate also doubled the auth type declarations TypeScript loads. AbsoluteJS now accepts auth up to 0.96. The `@absolutejs/auth/client/mobile` API it uses is byte-identical from 0.76.3 to 0.96.0, in both its declarations and its runtime.
changes.summary: Projects on a current `@absolutejs/auth` no longer get a second, older copy

changes.detail: Elysia 2 hands every open, message and close event of a WebSocket a new wrapper object. The dev server tracked HMR clients by that wrapper, so a closed browser tab was never removed (it stayed until a broadcast send threw) and each `ready` message counted the same tab again under `connectedTargets`, so `/hmr-status` reported clients that were gone and more web targets than open sockets. Clients are now tracked by the underlying socket.
changes.summary: `/hmr-status` no longer counts closed or duplicate HMR clients

changes.detail: Under `bun --hot`, Bun counts unhandled rejections that no listener claims and never resets the count; while it is non-zero Bun parks the process in a loop that still serves requests and delivers file-watch events but never runs timers. The server entry imports React pages, so saving a React component with a syntax error made Bun's hot reload reject, and from then on the HMR debounce never fired: every edit was detected and queued, including the one that fixed the error, and nothing rebuilt until the dev server restarted. An unhandled rejection in app code did the same. The dev server now claims unhandled rejections and prints them as before, so its timers keep running.
changes.summary: `absolute dev` keeps rebuilding after a syntax error in a React component or an unhandled rejection

changes.detail: `absolute bun-patch install` and the `absolute dev` offer now install `bun-v1.4.0-absolute.2`. The first release was built as a Bun canary build (Bun's build default): it reported `1.4.0-canary.1`, enabled Bun's experimental "bake" server features and made `bun upgrade` track canary. absolute.2 is built with `--canary=off`, as Bun's own releases are; the React Fast Refresh fix is unchanged. Run `absolute bun-patch install` to replace an absolute.1 install.
changes.summary: The patched Bun is now a release build, not a canary build

changes.detail: Stock Bun ignores `reactFastRefresh` on `Bun.Transpiler` (oven-sh/bun#32919), so React edits in `absolute dev` remounted the page and lost component state. AbsoluteJS now publishes Bun 1.4.0 with just that fix for every platform Bun ships (github.com/absolutejs/patched-bun). In React projects on stock Bun, `absolute dev` offers it once (Install now / Ask me later / Don't ask again); it installs to ~/.absolutejs/bun, is checked against a pinned SHA-256, and only the dev server uses it, so your `bun` is unchanged. `absolute bun-patch [status|install|remove|reset]` manages it; `ABSOLUTE_PATCHED_BUN=0` opts out.
changes.summary: React Fast Refresh keeps component state: `absolute dev` can run on AbsoluteJS's patched Bun

changes.detail: The React HMR client had a CSS-only branch that looked up the example app's `ReactExampleCSS` manifest key, so it could never work in another app; the server never sends a CSS-only React update, so it was also unreachable. Removed. Stylesheet edits on React pages go through the general stylesheet swap, now covered by a browser test (the rule applies, component state and the document are kept).
changes.summary: Removed a React HMR CSS branch that only matched the example app

changes.detail: The React fast path told the browser to re-import a single module: the first non-page file in the batch. A new component added to the page re-imported only the new file, so the page never rendered it; a folder created alongside a file became the target and its URL failed to load; and an edited hook or utility whose importer had not been fetched through the module server re-imported just itself, which updates nothing on screen. Every edited file now gets a target (hooks and utilities resolve to the nearest importing component, falling back to the dependents the dependency graph found), directories and deleted paths are skipped, and the client imports them all before refreshing. On stock Bun the remount fallback rendered the changed child in place of the whole page; it now re-imports the page module for the page on screen and ignores edits that do not reach it.
changes.summary: React edits that add a component, touch a hook or utility, or create a folder now update the page in place

changes.detail: The dev server decides between React Fast Refresh and the stock-Bun remount fallback by transpiling a probe component. The probe was named `__AbsoluteRefreshProbe`; React Fast Refresh registers only capitalized components, so it reported "unsupported" even on a Bun with the reactFastRefresh fix, and React edits always remounted with a warning. It now uses a capitalized name.
changes.summary: React Fast Refresh is used when Bun supports it, instead of always falling back to a remount

changes.detail: A React edit that failed to compile was still broadcast as an update. The browser imported a module that answered 500 and fell back to a full reload, which showed the last good page and no error. The dev server now checks the edited modules compile first and sends the error overlay (file, line and source line) instead; the save that fixes it applies as a normal in-place update. The module server handler and its transform errors also moved to globalThis: after a `bun --hot` reload failed part-way, later imports of the module server got a fresh instance that was never configured, so pre-transforming the changed module silently did nothing.
changes.summary: A syntax error in a React component shows the error overlay instead of reloading the page

changes.detail: Snapshot alt, title, placeholder and aria-label alongside SSR text. Temporarily restore those attributes and newly inserted text-only font trees while the framework hydrates, then reapply translations on the hydrated nodes. Preserve authored and interactive markup, URLs, field values and genuine client changes. Fixes translated landing-page warnings and text reverting to English without suppressing ordinary hydration mismatches.
changes.summary: Preserve browser-translated attributes and inserted text-only font wrappers through hydration

changes.detail: The engine is picked from the URL scheme (with drizzle.config dialect / Prisma provider as a fallback): PostgreSQL and CockroachDB, MySQL, MariaDB and SingleStore, SQLite and local libSQL files, remote libSQL/Turso (optional peer @libsql/client) and SQL Server (optional peer mssql). Dependency order, identifier quoting, upserts and value encoding are per dialect; generated columns are skipped and identity columns are inserted explicitly. MongoDB and Gel are refused with a clear message. `absolute db seed --url` hands the URL and engine to the seed script. PostgreSQL backups keep their exact file shape.
changes.summary: `absolute db backup` and `restore` work on every SQL engine Drizzle and Prisma support, not only PostgreSQL

changes.detail: json/jsonb values were stringified before binding, and Bun SQL JSON-encodes bound values, so every document was restored as a JSON string scalar. Array columns failed to bind, bytea values are now decoded from their backed-up Buffer JSON, `generated always` identity and generated columns were rejected, and serial/identity sequences were left behind the restored ids so the next insert collided.
changes.summary: `absolute db restore` into PostgreSQL keeps JSON documents, arrays, bytea, identity columns and sequences intact

changes.detail: `absolute start`, `compile`, the config server and `workspace` cleared their port by killing every process listening on it, including unrelated services and other projects' servers (a PostgreSQL, another app, a control plane). They now stop only a leftover AbsoluteJS server started from this project directory, and report anything else on the port as left running.
changes.summary: Starting a server no longer kills unrelated processes that hold its port
Apply the incremental asset rewrite fix to HTMX pages as well as HTML and verify both adapters with real builds
Reissue the tested HTML asset and OpenAPI fixes after npm left beta.118 unavailable with a phantom staged-version conflict
Preserve compiled HTML asset URLs during unrelated incremental page builds and prevent markup URL matching across adjacent tags; use the compatible fixed OpenAPI package

changes.detail: Recursive HMR paths could include a directory before .absolutejs-hmr files, bypass the basename-only filter, and restart the development server repeatedly. Generated snapshots now bypass editor atomic-write recovery in all three watcher paths; ordinary source edits still trigger HMR.
changes.summary: Ignore generated server snapshots at every watch depth and avoid treating their creation as an editor save.

changes.detail: Declare the jiti config loader dependency, build nested vendor fixtures inside the test, and reject missing native release arguments before loading application configuration. Normalize existing release-fixture lint issues without weakening checks.
changes.summary: Make clean CLI builds and release checks self-contained.

changes.detail: Create only a missing scaffold index so Capacitor completes its initial platform sync, without replacing compiled web assets or manufacturing a release manifest. Existing platform directories are synchronized on retry instead of failing a second add. Native initialization uses the current pinned Devices packages in the freshly built CLI.
changes.summary: Initialize native app targets before the first bundle and safely retry existing projects.

changes.detail: Generated TypeScript declaration aliases no longer bypass Expo runtime resolution. Archive identity and per-file checks reject corrupt data and repair stale cached files. The supported Android WebView extension keeps local assets offline and the native bridge origin-scoped without TLS exceptions or dependency patches. Expo runtime fingerprints require a new native binary. Installed Android acceptance now verifies fresh trusted-server props and exactly-once offline Sync reconciliation for both engines; iOS requires the separate partner checks.
changes.summary: Fix Expo Android embedded startup with a scoped HTTPS asset host, one runtime asset registry, verified archive extraction, and readiness after rendering.
Stabilize the existing UserAgentProvider declaration with an explicit provider type so inferred union ordering cannot cause spurious API changes.
Wait for Android network services before installed offline acceptance; add two-revision Capacitor and Expo branding conformance with packaged-pixel verification and light/dark screenshot evidence.

changes.detail: A typed mobile.branding contract now projects validated source PNGs into Capacitor and Expo icons, Android adaptive and themed layers, iOS appearance variants, and light/dark launch screens without application-authored native code. The mobile assets command wraps the pinned official Capacitor generator, installs it only as a direct development dependency when needed, previews artwork, records a content-addressed non-secret manifest, resumes platform-specific generation, reports bounded telemetry, and makes configured stale or missing output fail release doctor.
changes.summary: Capacitor and Expo share a first-class native branding pipeline

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS fsyncs and atomically installs a bounded non-secret promotion operation before contacting GitHub, advances the same identity through exact run discovery, completion and audit, lists local operations, and resumes persisted intent after sleep, disconnect or process failure without issuing another workflow dispatch.
changes.summary: Mobile CI promotions survive local interruption without duplicate dispatch

changes.detail: The promotion CLI assigns each protected dispatch a unique non-secret identity, discovers only the GitHub Actions run carrying that identity, returns its run ID and URL, optionally waits for completion, and can chain an independent local audit without racing concurrent promotions; retained format-1 audit context remains readable.
changes.summary: Mobile CI promotions correlate, watch, and audit the exact dispatched workflow run

changes.detail: `absolute mobile ci status` reports or watches a bounded GitHub run identity, while `absolute mobile ci audit` downloads the exact retained AAB or IPA and promotion evidence, re-hashes the release, re-verifies installed-app certification and Sigstore provenance, validates the publication receipt, and emits sanitized reproducible reports without credentials.
changes.summary: Mobile CI gains first-class promotion status and independent artifact auditing

changes.detail: A protected follow-up GitHub workflow restores a selected prior-run AAB or IPA without rebuilding, re-hashes it, verifies imported installed-app certification, signs the exact certification with GitHub OIDC and pinned Cosign, requires trusted registry provenance, publishes the existing artifact, and retains the final audit receipt.
changes.summary: Mobile CI resumes and promotes exact certified artifacts with portable Sigstore provenance
Mobile publication promotes the exact certified AAB or IPA with secure production policies and generated acceptance CI
Keep package-owned Vue components and helpers inside separate browser and server output trees, preserving relative imports, cache restoration and hot-reload identities.

changes.detail: `absolute mobile certify` revalidates immutable Android and iOS releases plus sanitized installed-app reports, binds the exact artifact, embedded runtime, app version, and evidence tier into an atomic content-addressed record, and verifies promotion policy without native tools or credentials. Android requires installed offline proof; iOS preserves the honest Simulator, registered-device, and Apple-processed TestFlight hierarchy.
changes.summary: Mobile releases gain content-addressed installed-app certification

changes.detail: Paired developer-owned Macs can now export and return the same-archive registered-device IPA, then execute source-equivalent Simulator, archive-equivalent registered-device, and store-delivered TestFlight acceptance from Windows or Linux. Protocol v4 atomically synchronizes and re-hashes immutable releases, validates returned evidence locally, propagates cancellation into Xcode and device tools, and emits sanitized remote-host reports and phase telemetry without transferring signing or publication credentials.
changes.summary: Remote Macs run all three installed iOS release acceptance lanes

changes.detail: `absolute mobile test ios --release` now records honest source-equivalent Simulator, same-archive registered-device, or Apple-processed TestFlight evidence. Capacitor and Expo emit version/build-specific native readiness markers, immutable releases can include a separately hashed registered-device IPA, physical offline claims require explicit confirmation, and sanitized reports retain only artifact classification, outcome, and bounded timings.
changes.summary: iOS releases gain three-lane installed-app acceptance

changes.detail: The provider-neutral release command now installs the exact Capacitor AAB-derived APK set on the managed emulator, takes both network transports offline, and requires an AbsoluteJS-owned native readiness signal across a cold launch and process relaunch. Bun workspace-hoisted Capacitor executables and package manifests are resolved only through the application’s governing workspace. Reports and telemetry retain only provider, artifact identity, outcome, and bounded timings.
changes.summary: Capacitor Android releases gain installed offline AAB acceptance

changes.detail: `absolute mobile test android --release` revalidates one immutable AAB, approval-installs checksum-pinned Bundletool, starts the managed emulator, installs the derived APK set, and proves embedded content across two offline process launches. Expo production web files travel through Metro as one deterministic opaque archive and are reconstructed from a verified offset table, avoiding per-file registry failures. Sanitized reports and telemetry record only artifact identity, sizes, timings, provider, and outcome.
changes.summary: Expo Android releases now have installed offline AAB acceptance

changes.detail: The exact public build command now resolves React vendor assets from linked packages, recognizes declared workspace lockfiles without trusting unrelated ancestors, avoids false-positive production HMR detection, prints per-phase timings, and verifies AAB signatures with translated paths through the Windows JDK. A permanent two-build gate validates signing, immutable metadata, all production ABIs, bundled JavaScript, release hygiene, and warm Gradle reuse.
changes.summary: WSL Expo Android releases now pass public-CLI conformance

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS projects generated in WSL build through a serialized Windows-local mirror with Windows Bun, a short temporary drive, full release ABIs, retained warm caches, sanitized phase telemetry, and the existing signing, doctor, immutable-artifact, and publishing contracts.
changes.summary: Expo Android production builds now run from WSL

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS retries a newly allocated loopback port without prompting, propagates the final port through local, WSL, and Remote Mac native targets, preserves it across rebuilds, and emits only a categorical reason plus bounded retry count.
changes.summary: Expo development recovers from Metro startup port races

changes.detail: An installed API 36 gate measures cold and warm launch, bridge and all-framework HMR p95, memory growth, native rebuild/reconnect, and native plus embedded-web accessibility while emitting only sanitized timing artifacts.
changes.summary: Expo Android development now has a performance and accessibility quality gate

changes.detail: Generated Expo shells forward a trusted, request-correlated native cancellation signal to the provider-neutral device lifecycle, while the installed API 36 gate covers camera and multi-photo success, cancellation, stale-result suppression, exactly-once delivery, and native-path redaction.
changes.summary: Expo Android picker recovery distinguishes explicit cancellation from delayed successful results

changes.detail: Generated Expo shells expose the provider-neutral restored-operation queue through the allowlisted bridge, and an installed API 36 gate proves exactly-once camera recovery without leaking native file paths.
changes.summary: Expo Android restores in-flight camera results after background process death

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS hashes the source lock input and invalidates the mirrored Windows lock only when dependencies change, avoiding repeated resolution while keeping each host Bun version in control of its own lock format.
changes.summary: WSL Expo Android rebuilds preserve a compatible Windows Bun lockfile until source dependencies change

changes.detail: Native inputs are fingerprinted and coalesced, local and Remote Mac sessions share a serialized rebuild contract, generated WebView hosts can select an AbsoluteJS path, native timing logs and telemetry remain data-minimal, and Android conformance verifies state preservation, rebuild, and reconnect.
changes.summary: Expo development now preserves one Metro process across automatic native rebuilds and provides installed-app HMR conformance for native React plus every supported embedded framework.

changes.detail: AbsoluteJS now lets Svelte's compiler-owned HMR wrapper complete its state restoration instead of racing it with a redundant remount.
changes.summary: Svelte rune state now remains deterministic across template-only HMR updates.
Expo iOS now has an automated native observability gate for generated Swift compilation, trusted-relay redaction, restart-safe retry, acknowledgement, and deduplication.
Expo iOS now has an automated installed-app replacement gate for native Auth, encrypted Sync migration, and exactly-once recovery.
Installed Expo iOS apps now have a production Simulator conformance gate for signed OTA safety, native Auth and Sync continuity, staged rollout controls, fleet recovery, and restart-safe reporting.
Installed Expo Android apps now exercise staged cohorts, automatic advancement, pause, resume, cancellation, fleet recovery, and restart-safe health reporting in the native conformance suite.
